_why: Strings rendered by the BACKEND, not by Compose. extract.py cannot find these — it scans app/src/main/java for Text()/label=/title= sites, and an edge function has none. So they are declared by hand here and MERGED into strings.json by extract.py, which keeps strings.json the single spec that check_lengths.py gates and generate.py compiles, and means re-running extraction never silently drops them. Add a string here the moment an edge function renders one.
_budgets: max_len is set explicitly rather than derived, because the tolerance formula in extract.py measures a Compose row or button and these strings live somewhere else. Push titles and bodies are measured against the Android notification tray (one title line, ~2 body lines); the rest is dialog and snackbar copy and carries the soft budget the extractor would have given it.
_placeholders: %1$s / %2$s, positional, matching the convention documented on Strings.kt: word order moves in translation and a translator must be free to reorder. supabase/functions/_shared/i18n.ts substitutes them the same way Kotlin's String.format does.
